sections.vendors: Sainsbury's published its refreshed Tier 1 GM & Clothing supplier list dated September 2026 on corporate.sainsburys.co.uk, confirming Babylon Garments, Talisman Ltd (two DEPZ Savar sites), Progress Apparels and Ayesha Fashion still active in Bangladesh, alongside Cambodia sites (New Wide Apparel, Genmei Industrial, Blossom Knitwear) and Sri Lanka (Miami Exports, Miami Clothing). No overt additions/exits of the named key vendors (Echotex, Kenpark, QUATTRO, SOUTH EAST TEXTILES, Paramount, SQ Birichina) were visible in this disclosure round.
sections.sustainability: The standout story: Sainsbury's joined M&S, New Look, Oxfam and Circle-8 on 23 September to launch 'The Circuit,' a UK circular-textiles initiative targeting end-of-use clothing. Phase one starts January 2027 at Oxfam's Batley, Yorkshire site, focused on automated sorting, traceability and fibre-to-fibre recycling routes, with Biffa, Ekman Group, Usha Yarns, Kipas, Reju and Worn Again Technologies as partners. This builds on Tu's existing 'Plan A for Another Life' ambition (5 million items given another life by 2030) and its recent cardboard-hanger swap in Tu Baby (5 million plastic hangers removed).
sections.strategy: Tu's Autumn/Winter 2026 womenswear is rolling out in phased monthly drops (September–December), described by Sainsbury's as its 'most elevated' collection yet, with premium knitwear expanded to include cashmere, mohair and alpaca alongside merino/lambswool. This continues the premiumisation push flagged since the April buying/merchandising restructure consultation, whose final outcome still hasn't been publicly confirmed as of this week.
sections.pricing: 86% of the new A/W26 womenswear range is priced under £30 and 65% under £25, preserving Tu's value positioning even as it adds premium fabrics (lambswool from £34, mohair from £45, cashmere from £69) — a deliberate 'accessible premium' architecture rather than a straight price rise.
sections.launches: A/W26 womenswear drops: warm neutrals and orange/brown tones in September, green shades and the main coat launch in October, red and embellished occasionwear in November ahead of festive season. Available via tu.co.uk, Argos and selected Sainsbury's stores.
sections.gossip: Trade press (Drapers, TheIndustry.fashion) framed the A/W26 collection launch as evidence Tu is chasing a more premium, fashion-credible position without abandoning value credentials — consistent with CEO Simon Roberts' repeated comments that clothing has 'outperformed the market.' No fresh commentary this week on the still-unresolved spring restructure.
soWhat: The Circuit puts Sainsbury's/Tu ahead of most mid-market rivals on end-of-life textile circularity — expect early supplier conversations on recycled-content fibre sourcing (rPET, mechanically/chemically recycled cotton) as the January 2027 Batley phase approaches.

The September 2026 Tier 1 list republish is a good checkpoint to verify your own factory's disclosure status and worker-representation data are current, since Sainsbury's audits against this list for onboarding/renewal decisions.

A/W26's expanded premium knitwear (cashmere, mohair, alpaca) signals real fibre-diversification demand beyond cotton/poly basics — mills with premium natural-fibre capability and reliable QC are the ones positioned to win incremental Tu volume this season.
